Customer account exists
Cart has items added
Storefront and xAPI accessible

   query { cart(storeId: "${STORE_ID}", cultureName: "en-US", currencyCode: "USD") { items { quantity productId } itemsCount } }

Admin logged in to Backend
Customer account exists

[HTTP] GET {{BACK_URL}}api/order/customerOrders/{id} using the denied-role token → confirm the payment's Total and the shipment's Price read 0 via the order route (baseline for comparison)
[HTTP] call the standalone Payment search/get endpoint discovered above, for the SAME payment id, using the SAME denied-role token
[HTTP] call the standalone Shipment search/get endpoint discovered above, for the SAME shipment id, using the SAME denied-role token

Title: A custom CanReadPrices override with no resolvable principal must deny, not throw a 500
Preconditions:
The sample module's SampleCustomerOrderDataProtectionService (or an equivalent custom CanReadPrices override) registered for ICustomerOrderDataProtectionService. Reach an order read with no resolvable user — a background job, an export, or an unauthenticated request that still reaches the service.
NOTE for the executing agent: re-reading the shipped diff for this run, SampleCustomerOrderDataProtectionService.CanReadPrices guards `user != null` BEFORE calling CanReadPricesForStore (the only caller of the unguarded FindPermission), and the BASE CustomerOrderDataProtectionService.CanReadPrices also short-circuits on `user is null` before touching claims. Both reachable paths appear to already guard the null case, which is INCONSISTENT with the "500 instead of deny" hypothesis this case was scaffolded to test — treat the assertion below as a genuine open question, not a known repro.
Steps:
[SETUP] Confirm the sample's SampleCustomerOrderDataProtectionService (or an equivalent custom CanReadPrices override) is registered as ICustomerOrderDataProtectionService in this environment; if not installed, exercise the BASE service's null-principal path instead (still meaningful — CustomerOrderDataProtectionService.CanReadPrices also short-circuits on user is null per the diff)
[HTTP] trigger an order read with NO resolvable principal reaching the protection service — the same system-context path used in ORDA-112 (a Hangfire job / no-HttpContext invocation), or an anonymous request if the route allows one to reach the service unauthenticated
[CAPTURE] the HTTP status code and response body
Cross_Layer_Checks: [EVENT] no unhandled-exception entry is logged for this request (Application Insights / platform exception log) — a logged NullReferenceException in ClaimsPrincipalExtensions.FindPermission would confirm the mechanism even if the HTTP layer masked it as a generic 500
Failure_Signals: HTTP 500 with a NullReferenceException / "Object reference not set" stack frame referencing FindPermission or CanReadPricesForStore; a 500 with no diagnostic body identifying the cause (still a defect against BL-AUTH-017, independent of root cause)

Title: Redacting a cache-owned order must not strip prices for the next entitled caller
Preconditions: Two users, one denied prices and one entitled. Read the SAME order as the denied user first, then immediately as the entitled user, with no cache eviction in between. Repeat for the nested shipment and payment, not just the order root.
Cross_Layer_Checks: [DB] a direct privileged GET well after any cache TTL confirms the stored order was never actually mutated, independent of timing
Failure_Signals: The entitled admin's read (taken right after the denied admin's read of the same order) shows 0/zeroed prices instead of the true values — the denied read's redaction leaked into a shared cached instance and poisoned the next entitled caller (pre-fix CustomerOrder.Clone() aliasing ChildrenOperations to the source's shipments/payments); the nested shipment or payment values also revert to zero on the entitled read while the order root shows true values (partial cache poisoning, proving the aliasing was one level down, not at the root)

Title: Granting order:read_prices takes effect on the next request with no sign-out
Preconditions: A denied-role admin user with an active session reading an order with prices masked. Then add order:read_prices to the ROLE (permissions live on roles, never on users) and re-read without signing out. Then remove it again and re-read.
Steps:
[NAV] {{ADMIN_URL}} sign in as the denied-role admin user (active session)
[HTTP] GET {{BACK_URL}}api/order/customerOrders/{id} using this session's token — confirm Total=0, withPrices=false
[NAV] {{ADMIN_URL}} in a SEPARATE admin session
[ACT] sign in as {{ADMIN_EMAIL}}
[ACT] add order:read_prices to the denied user's ROLE (Admin > Security > Roles — permissions live on the role, never the user, per VC-B2B-002)
[WAIT] the role update save confirmation appears
[HTTP] WITHOUT signing the first user out, repeat GET {{BACK_URL}}api/order/customerOrders/{id} using the SAME still-active session
[ACT] remove order:read_prices from the role again
[SAVE] confirm the role update is saved
[HTTP] repeat the GET once more with the same still-active session
Assertions:
[BODY] after the role grant, the SAME active session's next GET returns the true non-zero Total and withPrices=true, with no sign-out/sign-in in between {BL}
[BODY] after the role is revoked again, the SAME active session's next GET returns Total=0 and withPrices=false, again with no sign-out/sign-in {BL}
Cross_Layer_Checks: [ADMIN] the Admin SPA order blade, left open in the first session's browser tab and refreshed (not re-logged-in) after the grant, shows the price without a new sign-in
Failure_Signals: The active session keeps returning zeroed prices after the grant until the user signs out and back in (stale permission cache); the active session keeps returning real prices after the revoke until re-login (a stale-permission leak in the worse direction)
References: VCST-3912 · Archetype:STALE · Technique:ST · Probe:VC-B2B-002 | Promoted: REG-2026-09-11-1616 (2026-09-11)

Title: Restoring a backup exported without prices must not overwrite the stored prices with zeros
Preconditions: A user holding platform:backuprestore:access/backup/storage but NOT order:read_prices. A DISPOSABLE order with a known non-zero total — this case destroys prices if the guard regresses, so it must never run against a shared fixture. Export as that user (the archive will carry every price 0.0 and withPrices false), then strip the archive to the single disposable order before restoring.
Steps:
[SETUP] a DISPOSABLE order with a known real Total and one known LineItem.Price, captured via a privileged GET as {{ADMIN_EMAIL}} before this case touches it
[SETUP] a user holding platform:backuprestore:access/backup/storage but NOT order:read_prices
[AUTH] POST {{BACK_URL}}connect/token as that user -> capture access_token
[HTTP] GET {{BACK_URL}}api/platform/export/manifest/new, tick VirtoCommerce.Orders, then POST {{BACK_URL}}api/platform/export with that manifest -> wait for the job, download the archive
[ASSERT] the archive's VirtoCommerce.Orders.json carries the disposable order with total 0.0 and withPrices false - if it does not, the export half regressed and this case cannot test the restore half
[SETUP] strip the archive to the single disposable order, so the restore can touch nothing else, and re-zip
[HTTP] POST {{BACK_URL}}api/assets?folderUrl=backups (multipart) to upload the stripped archive -> capture relativeUrl
[HTTP] POST {{BACK_URL}}api/platform/import as {{ADMIN_EMAIL}} with fileUrl set to that relativeUrl and the full exportManifest object -> wait for the restore job to finish
[HTTP] GET {{BACK_URL}}api/order/customerOrders/{id} as {{ADMIN_EMAIL}} to read the stored order back
Cross_Layer_Checks:
[ADMIN] the disposable order reopened in the Admin SPA after the restore shows its original prices, not a masked or zeroed total
[DB] the privileged GET is taken after the job reports finished, not while it is running, so the read is of persisted state
Failure_Signals: The disposable order's Total or LineItem.Price reads back as 0 after the restore - a routine backup restore silently destroyed stored prices while the job reported success; or a control order outside the archive changed, meaning the import is not the per-entity upsert it is documented to be
Cleanup: Delete the disposable order and remove the uploaded archive from Backup storage. Never restore an unstripped price-free archive on a shared environment — it would zero every order it carries.
